advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether edit should surface a no-op confirmation when edit_core writes nothing, and align its behavior with the mutation contract.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:667: `_confirm.emit("edited", ticket_id, names, f"edited {ticket_id}: {names}")`
edit_core only appends an EDIT event `if out:` (src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:569) — an empty/unchanged edit writes nothing but the CLI still prints 'edited'
contract (_confirm.py:5): 'no change: <reason> on an idempotent no-op'
advisory.finding: The edit verb always emits an 'edited' confirmation even when edit_core commits nothing durable (e.g. fields whose values equal the current state, or tag ops that are no-ops), so the kubectl-style contract's 'no change: <reason>' branch is never reachable for edit despite the contract promising it for idempotent no-ops.

At e2e_field_validation_probe.sh:1003 the captured value is validated with `is_valid_ticket_id "$EPIC_LOCAL_ID"`, which will now fail on the summary line `created <alias> (<id>): <title>`
advisory.finding: `rebar create` (and `rebar idea`) no longer prints the trailing bare-id line in text mode; production probe scripts that capture the new id via `rebar create ... | tail -1` now capture the human summary line instead of the bare id, breaking at runtime.
scenarios: Running the jira-pressure-test e2e probes after this change: every `create ... | tail -1` captures the summary line, id validation fails, phases abort
advisory.suggested_fix: Update the probe scripts to pass `-o json` to `rebar create` and extract `.id` (as README/adapters were migrated), or have them parse the id out of the new `created ... (<id>): ...` line via regex.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm no external consumer relies on `rebar session-log`'s former unconditional `{id,alias,created}` JSON stdout, since it now defaults to text and its `-o json` envelope renames `id`->`subject` and drops `alias`/`created`.
evidence: Old CLI unconditionally emitted the raw result: replaced line `print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False))` (diff) which serialized `{"id", "alias", "created"}` (session_log.py:206 return of append/start)

New default prints a text confirmation via `_confirm_session_log`; `--output json` yields the uniform envelope keyed `subject`, not `id` — tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_session_log_capture.py:164 now reads `json.loads(out)["subject"]`

`session-log` is in `_WRITES_FULL` (src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:140) hence `_CONFIRM_SCOPE`, but NOT in `_LEGACY_OUTPUT` (src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:_LEGACY_OUTPUT = create/idea/transition/claim/reopen), so its prior JSON shape is not preserved
ABSENCE: no in-repo production (non-test) consumer of the old `session-log` JSON stdout was found via grep of `session-log`, so no runtime callsite is cited
advisory.finding: `rebar session-log` changed its default stdout from an unconditional machine-readable JSON dict {id, alias, created} to a human text line, and its `--output json` shape to the new envelope {outcome, subject, detail} (id renamed to subject; alias/created dropped) without being placed in the legacy-JSON-preserving set.
scenarios: An external script that ran `rebar session-log append ... ` and parsed `json.loads(stdout)["id"]` or `["created"]` now gets no JSON by default, and under `-o json` finds `subject` instead of `id` and no `created` field

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm no consumer depends on session-log's former default raw-JSON stdout; document the output change in release notes / migration guidance.
evidence: old: `-    print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False))`
new: `+    _confirm_session_log(verb, result)` routes to text line by default and to the truncated envelope under --output json
session-log is in _WRITES_FULL (src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:140) and is NOT in _LEGACY_OUTPUT (src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:433), so no byte-identical JSON guarantee applies
dropped.finding: session-log previously printed its full raw JSON result (print(json.dumps(result))) on stdout unconditionally; the change makes the default output a text line and, under --output json, emits only the uniform {outcome,subject,detail} envelope rather than the prior full result shape. Any existing script parsing session-log's default stdout as JSON breaks.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a capsys/redirect_stdout test asserting the library facade (rebar.archive(), and the other widened leaf callers) writes nothing to stdout, pinning the 'library/MCP callers stay print-free' contract the leaf.py/_confirm.py docstrings claim.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py:197 docstring: 'the former in-seam ``Archived ticket`` print moved there, so library/MCP callers no longer get a stray stdout line'
src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py:219 `def archive(ticket_id, *, repo_root=None) -> None:` calls `_python_leaf(leaf.archive, ...)` in-process (no CLI confirmation context)
tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py:120-175 call `rebar.archive(tid, repo_root=...)` in-process but assert only on-disk snapshot/marker state, never captured stdout

ABSENCE: no capsys-based assertion in tests/unit/test_mutation_confirmations.py (search for 'capsys' returned no matches) and no test grepping for 'Archived ticket' / a print-free library path (search returned only src + docs hits)
dropped.finding: The migration moves leaf.archive's former in-seam `print(f"Archived ticket '{resolved}'")` (and normalizes comment/tag/untag/set_file_impact/set_verify_commands to return values instead of printing) with the explicit contract that library/MCP callers stay print-free — but no test asserts the LIBRARY facade path (rebar.archive() and the other in-process leaf callers) emits nothing on stdout. All mutation-confirmation assertions go through the CLI subprocess; test_scan_scoping.py exercises rebar.archive() in-process but never captures stdout. A regression re-adding an in-seam print (the exact bug the _confirm.py docstring warns corrupts MCP's JSON-RPC stdio) would not be caught.
scenarios: A future refactor of leaf.archive re-introduces an in-seam stdout print
MCP archive_ticket / library rebar.archive() invoked over rebar-mcp's JSON-RPC stdio
dropped.suggested_fix: In an in-process test, wrap `rebar.archive(tid, repo_root=...)` (and rebar.comment/tag) in `contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO())` or use capsys and assert the captured stdout is empty, both on the write and idempotent-no-op paths.
